Due Date: Annual — on or before 30 September of the immediate next financial year for DIN holders covered by Rule 12A.
Statutory Reference: Rule 12A Companies (Appointment and Qualification of Directors) Rules, 2014
Penalty: DIN may be deactivated for non-filing; ₹5,000 fee applies for delayed KYC filing.

Compliance: DIR-3 KYC-WEB — annual web-based director KYC
Due Date: Annual — on or before 30 September of the immediate next financial year for DIN holders covered by Rule 12A.
Statutory Reference: Rule 12A Companies (Appointment and Qualification of Directors) Rules, 2014
Penalty: DIN may be deactivated for non-filing; ₹5,000 fee applies for delayed KYC filing.

Due Date: Event-based — within 30 days of appointment
Statutory Reference: Section 170(2) Companies Act, 2013 r/w Rule 18 Companies (Appointment and Qualification of Directors) Rules, 2014
Penalty: Additional filing fee and penalties may apply for delayed or omitted filing.

Compliance: MBP-1 — disclosure of interest by director
Due Date: Annual / event-based — at the first Board meeting attended, at the first Board meeting of each financial year, and whenever the disclosure changes
Statutory Reference: Section 184(1) Companies Act, 2013
Penalty: Contravention may attract monetary penalty on the director and can affect validity of interested transactions.

Compliance: DIR-11 — notice of resignation by director
Due Date: Event-based — may be filed by the resigning director within 30 days of resignation
Statutory Reference: Section 168(1) Companies Act, 2013 r/w Rule 15 Companies (Appointment and Qualification of Directors) Rules, 2014
Penalty: Additional filing fee may apply for late filing; company-side DIR-12 compliance remains separate.

Compliance: DIR-12 — company reporting of director resignation
Due Date: Event-based — within 30 days of resignation / cessation
Statutory Reference: Section 170(2) Companies Act, 2013 r/w Rule 18 Companies (Appointment and Qualification of Directors) Rules, 2014
Penalty: Additional filing fee and statutory penalties may apply for default.

Due Date: Event-based — DIR-12 generally within 30 days of appointment / reappointment
Statutory Reference: Sections 152 and 170 Companies Act, 2013 r/w Rule 18 Companies (Appointment and Qualification of Directors) Rules, 2014
Penalty: Additional filing fee and statutory penalties may apply for default.

Due Date: Annual / event-based — at the first Board meeting in which the director participates, at the first Board meeting of each financial year, and whenever circumstances change
Statutory Reference: Section 149(7) Companies Act, 2013
Penalty: No separate filing penalty; non-compliance is dealt with under the applicable substantive provision.

Due Date: Event-based — follow the statutory notice and election process; DIR-12 generally within 30 days of appointment
Statutory Reference: Section 151 Companies Act, 2013 r/w Rule 7 Companies (Appointment and Qualification of Directors) Rules, 2014
Penalty: Additional filing fee and statutory penalties may apply if appointment-related filings are delayed.

Due Date: Event-based — appointment by Board; DIR-12 generally within 30 days. A KMP vacancy is to be filled within six months
Statutory Reference: Section 203 Companies Act, 2013 r/w Rules 8 and 8A Companies (Appointment and Remuneration of Managerial Personnel) Rules, 2014
Penalty: Contravention attracts penalties on the company and officers in default under Section 203.

Due Date: Event-based / annual — approvals must be in place before payment or appointment; annual disclosures form part of corporate reporting
Statutory Reference: Section 197 Companies Act, 2013 r/w Schedule V
Penalty: Excess remuneration may be recoverable and contravention can attract statutory penalties.

Compliance: MR-1 — return of appointment of MD / WTD / Manager
Due Date: Event-based — within 60 days of appointment
Statutory Reference: Section 196 Companies Act, 2013 r/w Rule 3 Companies (Appointment and Remuneration of Managerial Personnel) Rules, 2014
Penalty: Additional filing fee and statutory penalties may apply for default.

Due Date: Annual — with the Board's Report and financial statements, as applicable
Statutory Reference: Section 197(12) Companies Act, 2013 r/w Rule 5 Companies (Appointment and Remuneration of Managerial Personnel) Rules, 2014
Penalty: No separate filing penalty; non-compliance is dealt with under the applicable substantive provision.

Due Date: Annual / event-based — at the AGM; DIR-12 generally within 30 days if there is an appointment or cessation to report
Statutory Reference: Section 152(6) Companies Act, 2013
Penalty: Additional filing fee and statutory penalties may apply where the required ROC filing is delayed.

Due Date: Governance / event-based — record participation and attendance for each Board meeting; no separate quarterly filing deadline. Board-meeting frequency is governed by Section 173.
Statutory Reference: Section 173 Companies Act, 2013
Penalty: No standalone filing penalty for participation/attendance records. Consequences depend on the specific Section 173 / governance default; do not apply ₹25,000 as a generic penalty.

Due Date: Annual / event-based — disclose interests at the first Board meeting of each financial year and whenever there is a change; transaction approvals are event-based
Statutory Reference: Sections 184 and 188 Companies Act, 2013
Penalty: Non-compliance can attract penalties and may make the transaction voidable / require ratification.

Due Date: Event-based — statutory conditions and approvals must be satisfied before the loan, guarantee or security is provided
Statutory Reference: Section 185 Companies Act, 2013
Penalty: Contravention can attract monetary penalties on the company, officers and recipient, and other statutory consequences.

Due Date: Annual — approved by the Board and circulated with the financial statements before the AGM
Statutory Reference: Section 134 Companies Act, 2013 r/w Companies (Accounts) Rules, 2014
Penalty: Contravention attracts penalties on the company and officers under Section 134.

Due Date: Annual — with the financial statements and Board's Report, as applicable
Statutory Reference: Sections 197 and 134 Companies Act, 2013 r/w applicable disclosure rules
Penalty: No separate filing penalty; non-compliance is dealt with under the applicable substantive provision.

Compliance: Register of directors and KMP — maintenance and updates
Due Date: Ongoing — update the statutory register when particulars change; keep it available as required
Statutory Reference: Section 170 Companies Act, 2013
Penalty: Default attracts statutory penalties under the Companies Act.

Compliance: Director disclosures — other directorships / disqualification status
Due Date: Annual / event-based — at the start of the financial year / first Board meeting and whenever particulars change
Statutory Reference: Sections 164 and 184 Companies Act, 2013 r/w applicable rules
Penalty: Incorrect or omitted disclosure may trigger director and company-level compliance consequences.

Due Date: Annual — 30 days after the AGM Date
Statutory Reference: Section 137 Companies Act, 2013 r/w Rule 12
Penalty: ₹100 per day with no cap, plus penalties on the company and every officer in default.

Due Date: Annual — 30 days after the AGM Date
Statutory Reference: Section 129(3) Companies Act, 2013 r/w Rule 6
Penalty: ₹100 per day with no cap.

Compliance: AOC-4 NBFC — filing of NBFC financial statements
Relevant Form / Document (best effort): AOC-4 NBFC (Ind AS) / applicable NBFC variant
Due Date: Annual — within 30 days of the AGM
Statutory Reference: Section 137 Companies Act, 2013 r/w applicable Companies (Accounts) / filing rules for NBFCs
Penalty: Additional filing fee applies for delay; continuing default can attract company and officer penalties.

Compliance: AOC-4 XBRL — financial statements in XBRL format
Due Date: Annual — 30 days after the AGM Date
Statutory Reference: Rule 3 Companies (Filing of Documents and Forms in XBRL) Rules, 2015
Penalty: ₹100 per day with no cap.

Due Date: Annual — 60 days after the AGM Date
Statutory Reference: Section 92 Companies Act, 2013 r/w Rule 11
Penalty: Additional filing fee ₹100 per day of delay under applicable filing-fee rules; separate statutory penalty under Section 92 may also apply.

Compliance: MGT-7A — annual return for OPC / small company
Due Date: Annual — 60 days after the AGM Date
Statutory Reference: Section 92 Companies Act, 2013 r/w Rule 11(1) proviso
Penalty: Additional filing fee ₹100 per day of delay under applicable filing-fee rules; separate statutory penalty under Section 92 may also apply.

Due Date: Annual — approved by the Board and sent with the financial statements before the AGM
Statutory Reference: Section 134 Companies Act, 2013 r/w Companies (Accounts) Rules, 2014
Penalty: Contravention attracts penalties on the company and officers under Section 134.

Compliance: Financial statements — preparation, approval and signing
Relevant Form / Document (best effort): Balance Sheet + Statement of Profit and Loss + Cash Flow + Notes, as applicable
Due Date: Annual — prepare for Board approval before circulation and AGM
Statutory Reference: Sections 129 and 134 Companies Act, 2013
Penalty: Non-compliance can attract penalties relating to financial statements and Board reporting.

Due Date: First AGM: within 9 months from close of first financial year. Thereafter: within 6 months from close of FY and not more than 15 months between AGMs; Registrar may extend a non-first AGM by up to 3 months.
Statutory Reference: Section 96 Companies Act, 2013
Penalty: Default in holding an AGM is punishable under Section 99. Keep the penalty amount/version as a law-versioned parameter rather than a fixed generic value.

Due Date: Annual — ordinarily at least 21 clear days before the AGM, unless shorter notice is validly consented to
Statutory Reference: Section 101 Companies Act, 2013
Penalty: Defective notice can invalidate proceedings and may attract statutory consequences.

Due Date: Event-based — minutes must be prepared, signed and entered in the minutes book within 30 days of the meeting
Statutory Reference: Section 118 Companies Act, 2013 r/w Secretarial Standard on General Meetings (SS-2)
Penalty: Default attracts penalties on the company and officers under Section 118.

Due Date: Annual — complete in time for filing MGT-7 / MGT-7A within 60 days of the AGM
Statutory Reference: Section 92 Companies Act, 2013 r/w Rule 11 Companies (Management and Administration) Rules, 2014
Penalty: Late filing attracts additional fee and penalties applicable to the annual return.

Due Date: Annual — 15 days after the AGM Date
Statutory Reference: Section 139 Companies Act, 2013 r/w Rule 4
Penalty: Additional fee applies under the Companies (Registration Offices and Fees) Rules, 2014; separate statutory consequences may apply. Do not use a universal ₹100/day penalty.

Due Date: Event-based — obtain before appointment / reappointment
Statutory Reference: Section 139(1) Companies Act, 2013 r/w Rule 4 Companies (Audit and Auditors) Rules, 2014
Penalty: Appointment made without the required eligibility / consent can be non-compliant and require corrective action.

Compliance: Auditor reappointment — AGM resolution and ROC filing
Due Date: Annual — 15 days after the AGM Date
Statutory Reference: Section 139 Companies Act, 2013 r/w Rule 4
Penalty: Additional fee applies under the Companies (Registration Offices and Fees) Rules, 2014; separate statutory consequences may apply. Do not use a universal ₹100/day penalty.

Due Date: Event-based — Board generally fills the vacancy within 30 days; where caused by resignation, shareholder approval is required within three months
Statutory Reference: Section 139(8) Companies Act, 2013
Penalty: Failure to fill the vacancy or complete required filings can attract statutory penalties and additional filing fees.

Due Date: Event-based — auditor to file within 30 days of resignation
Statutory Reference: Section 140(2) Companies Act, 2013 r/w Rule 8 Companies (Audit and Auditors) Rules, 2014
Penalty: Late or non-filing can attract statutory penalty on the auditor in addition to filing fees.

Compliance: Independent auditor's report — completion and signing
Due Date: Annual — completed and signed with the audited financial statements before circulation / AGM
Statutory Reference: Section 143 Companies Act, 2013
Penalty: Professional and statutory consequences apply for non-compliance or defective reporting.

Compliance: Secretarial audit — MR-3 for prescribed companies
Due Date: Annual — annex to the Board's Report for the relevant financial year
Statutory Reference: Section 204 Companies Act, 2013 r/w Rule 9 Companies (Appointment and Remuneration of Managerial Personnel) Rules, 2014
Penalty: Contravention attracts penalties on the company, officers and practising company secretary under Section 204.

Due Date: Annual / event-based — appoint early enough to complete the statutory secretarial audit before the Board's Report is finalised
Statutory Reference: Section 204 Companies Act, 2013 r/w applicable rules
Penalty: No separate filing penalty; failure to obtain the required secretarial audit attracts Section 204 consequences.

Compliance: MGT-8 — certification of annual return, where applicable
Due Date: Annual — obtain before filing the annual return; MGT-7 is due within 60 days of the AGM
Statutory Reference: Section 92(2) Companies Act, 2013 r/w Rule 11 Companies (Management and Administration) Rules, 2014
Penalty: Incorrect certification or failure to obtain required certification can attract statutory and professional penalties.

Due Date: Annual — finalise for inclusion in MGT-7 / MGT-7A within the annual-return filing timeline
Statutory Reference: Section 92 Companies Act, 2013 r/w Companies (Management and Administration) Rules, 2014
Penalty: Incorrect or omitted annual-return particulars may attract penalties applicable to the annual return.

Relevant Form / Document (best effort): Promoter Holding Statement / annual return data
Due Date: Annual — update and reconcile for annual-return and financial-statement disclosures
Statutory Reference: Sections 88 and 92 Companies Act, 2013 r/w applicable rules
Penalty: No separate filing penalty; non-compliance is dealt with under the applicable substantive provision.

Compliance: Register / list of members — annual return support
Relevant Form / Document (best effort): List of Members / Register of Members
Due Date: Ongoing / annual — maintain continuously and reconcile for the annual return
Statutory Reference: Sections 88 and 92 Companies Act, 2013
Penalty: Default in maintenance or annual-return reporting attracts penalties under the relevant provisions.

Compliance: Director and KMP details — annual return disclosure
Due Date: Annual — reconcile for the annual return and update event-based changes through applicable ROC forms
Statutory Reference: Sections 170 and 92 Companies Act, 2013
Penalty: No separate filing penalty; non-compliance is dealt with under the applicable substantive provision.

Relevant Form / Document (best effort): Remuneration Statement / financial statements / Board's Report
Due Date: Annual — with the financial statements and Board's Report, as applicable
Statutory Reference: Section 197 Companies Act, 2013 r/w applicable rules
Penalty: No separate filing penalty; non-compliance is dealt with under the applicable substantive provision.

Compliance: Board meetings — statutory frequency and gap
Due Date: First Board meeting within 30 days of incorporation; thereafter at least 4 Board meetings every year with not more than 120 days between consecutive meetings. Special rules apply to OPC/small/dormant companies.
Statutory Reference: Section 173 Companies Act, 2013
Penalty: Section 173 consequences depend on the specific default. The ₹25,000 amount in Section 173(4) relates to failure by an officer to give required notice and is not a generic meeting-frequency penalty.

Due Date: Governance / event-based — maintain attendance for each Board meeting; no standalone quarterly filing due date.
Statutory Reference: Section 173 Companies Act, 2013
Penalty: No standalone filing penalty for the attendance record itself; apply the consequence of the actual underlying governance default, if any.

Compliance: Statutory committee meetings — scheduling, attendance and minutes
Due Date: Periodic / event-based — frequency depends on the committee, company class and applicable law / listing requirements
Statutory Reference: Companies Act, 2013 and applicable committee rules / Secretarial Standards
Penalty: Penalties depend on the specific committee obligation and applicable law.

Relevant Form / Document (best effort): CSR-2 where applicable + Board's Report disclosures
Due Date: Annual — complete CSR spending / transfer / reporting obligations for the financial year and make prescribed filings / disclosures
Statutory Reference: Section 135 Companies Act, 2013 r/w Companies (Corporate Social Responsibility Policy) Rules, 2014
Penalty: Unspent-amount and reporting defaults can attract monetary penalties under Section 135.

Compliance: CSR — annual report and Board's Report disclosure
Due Date: Annual — included in / annexed to the Board's Report for the financial year
Statutory Reference: Section 135 Companies Act, 2013 r/w Rule 8 Companies (Corporate Social Responsibility Policy) Rules, 2014
Penalty: No separate filing penalty; non-compliance is dealt with under the applicable substantive provision.

Compliance: AOC-2 — disclosure of related-party contracts / arrangements, where applicable
Due Date: Annual — annexed to the Board's Report for the relevant financial year
Statutory Reference: Section 134(3)(h) Companies Act, 2013 r/w Rule 8(2) Companies (Accounts) Rules, 2014 and Section 188
Penalty: Underlying related-party transaction defaults can attract penalties and require ratification / restitution.

Compliance: Loans, guarantees, securities and investments — Section 186 compliance
Due Date: Event-based — obtain required approvals before the transaction and update the statutory register promptly
Statutory Reference: Section 186 Companies Act, 2013
Penalty: Contravention can attract penalties on the company and officers in default.

Compliance: DPT-3 — annual return of deposits / exempt receipts
Due Date: Annual — on or before 30 June every year for information as on 31 March, subject to MCA extensions.
Statutory Reference: Rule 16 Companies (Acceptance of Deposits) Rules, 2014
Penalty: Additional filing fee and statutory consequences apply under the Companies (Acceptance of Deposits) Rules / MCA fee rules; do not use a single universal penalty amount.

Compliance: MSME-1 — half-yearly return of outstanding dues to micro and small enterprises
Due Date: Half Yearly — generally 30 April for October–March and 31 October for April–September
Statutory Reference: Section 405 Companies Act, 2013 r/w Specified Companies (Furnishing of Information about Payment to Micro and Small Enterprise Suppliers) Order, 2019
Penalty: Non-filing / incorrect filing can attract penalties under Section 405.

Compliance: BEN-2 — return of significant beneficial ownership
Due Date: Event-based — company to file within 30 days of receipt of the BEN-1 declaration
Statutory Reference: Section 90 Companies Act, 2013 r/w Companies (Significant Beneficial Owners) Rules, 2018
Penalty: Company and officer defaults can attract monetary penalties; SBO-related restrictions may also apply.

Compliance: PAS-6 — reconciliation of share capital audit
Due Date: Half Yearly — within 60 days from the conclusion of each half-year, where applicable
Statutory Reference: Rules 9A / 9B Companies (Prospectus and Allotment of Securities) Rules, 2014, as applicable
Penalty: Late filing attracts additional fee and statutory penalties may apply.

Compliance: Annual return — website disclosure and Board's Report link
Due Date: Annual — place the annual return on the company's website, if any, and disclose the web-link in the Board's Report
Statutory Reference: Section 92(3) Companies Act, 2013
Penalty: Default is dealt with under the annual-return / Board-report compliance provisions.

Compliance: Statutory registers — annual review and continuous update
Due Date: Ongoing — maintain and update the applicable statutory registers when the triggering event occurs; no universal annual filing due date.
Statutory Reference: Sections 85, 88, 170, 189 Companies Act, 2013
Penalty: Penalty depends on the particular register/default and applicable section; do not use a single universal amount.

Due Date: Annual / ongoing — no standalone filing; review before annual filings and AGM
Statutory Reference: Companies Act, 2013 and rules applicable to the relevant statutory records
Penalty: No separate filing penalty; non-compliance is dealt with under the applicable substantive provision.

Due Date: Event-based — final dividend is declared at the AGM; declared dividend is generally payable within 30 days
Statutory Reference: Sections 123 and 127 Companies Act, 2013
Penalty: Failure to distribute declared dividend within the statutory period can attract interest and penalties under Section 127.

Due Date: Event-based — unpaid amount is transferred to the Unpaid Dividend Account within 7 days after expiry of 30 days from declaration; further IEPF timelines then apply
Statutory Reference: Section 124 Companies Act, 2013 r/w IEPF Authority Rules, 2016
Penalty: Company and officer penalties apply for failure to transfer / report amounts as required.

Compliance: IEPF-4 — statement of shares transferred to IEPF
Due Date: Event-based — file within 30 days of the corporate action effecting transfer of shares to the IEPF demat account
Statutory Reference: Section 124(6) Companies Act, 2013 r/w Rule 6 IEPF Authority (Accounting, Audit, Transfer and Refund) Rules, 2016
Penalty: Default can attract penalties under the Companies Act / IEPF Rules.

Compliance: IEPF-5 claim — company verification and records
Due Date: Event-based — company/bank must submit the IEPF-5 e-verification report within 30 days from the date of submission of the claim.
Statutory Reference: Rule 7 IEPF Authority (Accounting, Audit, Transfer and Refund) Rules, 2016
Penalty: Additional fee of ₹50 per day applies after the prescribed period, subject to a maximum of ₹2,500, as stated in the current MCA instruction kit.

Compliance: Annual compliance certificate — internal / engagement deliverable
Due Date: Annual / internal — no universal standalone ROC filing due date
Statutory Reference: Internal governance / professional engagement requirement; statutory basis depends on the certificate used
Penalty: No standalone statutory penalty unless the certificate is required under a specific provision.

Compliance: Director annual declarations — interest and disqualification status
Due Date: Annual / event-based — collect at the first Board meeting / start of the financial year and on changes, as applicable
Statutory Reference: Sections 164 and 184 Companies Act, 2013 r/w applicable rules
Penalty: Incorrect or missing declarations can trigger director and company-level compliance consequences.

Compliance: Auditor independence and eligibility — annual / appointment check
Due Date: Annual / event-based — verify before appointment / reappointment and monitor throughout the engagement
Statutory Reference: Sections 139 and 141 Companies Act, 2013
Penalty: Ineligible appointment and prohibited relationships can require vacancy / corrective action and may attract penalties.

Compliance: Financial statements — Board approval and signing
Due Date: Annual — Board approval and prescribed signatures before circulation and AGM
Statutory Reference: Section 134(1) Companies Act, 2013
Penalty: Non-compliance can attract penalties under Section 134.

Compliance: ROC annual filing — reconciliation and completeness check
Due Date: Annual / internal — complete before AOC-4 and MGT-7 / MGT-7A filings
Statutory Reference: Internal control supporting Sections 92 and 137 Companies Act, 2013
Penalty: No separate filing penalty; non-compliance is dealt with under the applicable substantive provision.

Due Date: Annual / internal — after completion of annual corporate filings and supporting reviews
Statutory Reference: Internal governance; no universal standalone statutory filing
Penalty: No separate filing penalty; non-compliance is dealt with under the applicable substantive provision.

Compliance: CSR-1 — registration of eligible CSR implementing entity
Due Date: Event-based — complete registration before undertaking CSR activities as an implementing agency
Statutory Reference: Rule 4(2) Companies (Corporate Social Responsibility Policy) Rules, 2014
Penalty: Without valid registration, the entity cannot act as an eligible implementing agency for covered CSR projects.

Compliance: CSR utilisation — certification of funds disbursed and used
Relevant Form / Document (best effort): Utilisation Certificate / CFO or responsible person certification
Due Date: Annual / ongoing — certify utilisation for Board review as part of CSR monitoring; no separate ROC filing date
Statutory Reference: Rule 4(5) Companies (Corporate Social Responsibility Policy) Rules, 2014
Penalty: No separate filing penalty; non-compliance is dealt with under the applicable substantive provision.

Compliance: CSR-2 — report on corporate social responsibility
Due Date: Annual — file CSR-2 for the relevant financial year within the timeline prescribed by Rule 12(1B) and the FY-specific MCA notification / filing mechanism; do not derive a universal 31 December rule without the applicable FY notification.
Statutory Reference: Rule 12(1B) Companies (Accounts) Rules, 2014
Penalty: Do not infer a CSR-2 filing penalty from Section 135 unspent-CSR penalties. Apply the current MCA filing-fee / statutory consequence for the relevant FY and default.

Due Date: Annual — include the prescribed CSR disclosures in the Board's Report for the financial year
Statutory Reference: Section 134(3)(o) and Section 135 Companies Act, 2013 r/w Rule 8 Companies (Corporate Social Responsibility Policy) Rules, 2014
Penalty: Reporting and unspent-amount defaults can attract penalties under Section 135 and related provisions.

Compliance: CSR — annual report on CSR activities
Due Date: Annual — prepare for inclusion / annexure to the Board's Report
Statutory Reference: Rule 8 Companies (Corporate Social Responsibility Policy) Rules, 2014
Penalty: No separate filing penalty; non-compliance is dealt with under the applicable substantive provision.

Compliance: EPF Form 5A — employer ownership / management particulars
Due Date: Event-based — furnish prescribed ownership / management particulars and update changes within the applicable EPFO timeline
Statutory Reference: Paragraph 36A EPF Scheme, 1952 / EPFO Form 5A requirements
Penalty: Failure to furnish required employer particulars can attract action under the EPF law and delay establishment services.

Due Date: Monthly — 1 month, up to day 15 of that month after end of the period
Statutory Reference: Para 38 EPF Scheme, 1952
Penalty: Delayed remittance can attract interest under Section 7Q and damages under Section 14B. The damages rate/policy has changed over time; calculate using the notification/policy effective for the default period rather than the legacy 5–100% table.

Compliance: EPF ECR and challan — monthly reconciliation
Due Date: Monthly / internal — complete after ECR filing and contribution payment for the month
Statutory Reference: Internal control supporting Paragraph 38 EPF Scheme, 1952
Penalty: No separate filing penalty; unresolved short payment can attract interest and damages.

Due Date: Event-based — complete on joining / before inclusion in the first applicable ECR
Statutory Reference: EPF Scheme, 1952 and EPFO UAN / member-enrolment process
Penalty: Omission can lead to contribution arrears, interest, damages and employee-service issues.

Compliance: UAN generation / allotment for eligible employee
Due Date: Event-based — complete on joining / before the first applicable ECR where a UAN does not already exist
Statutory Reference: EPFO UAN / member-registration requirements under the EPF Scheme
Penalty: Delay can cause ECR / KYC / benefit-processing issues and contribution reconciliation problems.

Compliance: Form 11 — employee declaration of previous EPF / UAN details
Due Date: Event-based — obtain at the time of joining before completing PF enrolment
Statutory Reference: EPF Scheme, 1952 / EPFO Form 11 requirements
Penalty: Incorrect or missing declaration can create duplicate UANs and contribution / service-history issues.

Compliance: EPF member KYC — onboarding and verification
Due Date: Event-based — complete during onboarding and update when KYC particulars change
Statutory Reference: EPFO UAN / KYC requirements
Penalty: Incomplete KYC can restrict online claims, transfers and other member services.

Compliance: EPF member date of exit — update
Relevant Form / Document (best effort): Date of Exit update on EPFO portal
Due Date: Event-based — update promptly after cessation of employment and before claim / transfer processing
Statutory Reference: EPFO member-service / employer portal requirements
Penalty: Delay can obstruct transfer, withdrawal and pension-related processing.

Due Date: Event-based — submit when an error or change is identified
Statutory Reference: EPFO member profile / joint declaration process
Penalty: No separate periodic penalty; incorrect profile data can block KYC, transfer or claim processing.

Due Date: Event-based — update when establishment particulars change or an error is identified
Statutory Reference: EPF Scheme, 1952 and EPFO employer portal requirements
Penalty: Interest at the statutory rate under the ESI Act / Regulations and damages under Regulation 31C based on the duration of default; retain the default-period slab rather than a single flat penalty.

Due Date: Monthly — 1 month, up to day 15 of that month after end of the period
Statutory Reference: Regulation 31 ESI (General) Regulations, 1950
Penalty: Interest at 12% a year plus damages up to 25% of the arrears.

Due Date: State-specific — due date varies by the applicable State / local professional-tax law, registration type and periodicity
Statutory Reference: Applicable State / local Professional Tax Act and Rules
Penalty: State-specific interest, late fee and penalty apply for delayed payment / return.

Due Date: State-specific — due date varies by the applicable State / local professional-tax law, registration type and periodicity
Statutory Reference: Applicable State / local Professional Tax Act and Rules
Penalty: State-specific interest, late fee and penalty apply for delayed payment / return.

Due Date: State-specific — due date varies by the applicable State / local professional-tax law, registration type and periodicity
Statutory Reference: Applicable State / local Professional Tax Act and Rules
Penalty: State-specific interest, late fee and penalty apply for delayed payment / return.

Due Date: State-specific — due date varies by the applicable State / local professional-tax law, registration type and periodicity
Statutory Reference: Applicable State / local Professional Tax Act and Rules
Penalty: State-specific interest, late fee and penalty apply for delayed payment / return.

Due Date: State-specific — due date varies by the applicable State / local professional-tax law, registration type and periodicity
Statutory Reference: Applicable State / local Professional Tax Act and Rules
Penalty: State-specific interest, late fee and penalty apply for delayed payment / return.

Compliance: Income tax return — person / institution filing ITR-7
Due Date: Annual — statutory due date depends on the category and audit requirement; file by the applicable due date under Section 139(1)
Statutory Reference: Section 139(1) r/w Sections 139(4A) to 139(4D), Income-tax Act
Penalty: Late filing can attract fee, interest and restrictions on carry-forward / exemption claims, as applicable.

Due Date: Annual — due date depends on audit applicability and the relevant tax period. Do not derive the product deadline from a fixed month-offset alone.
Statutory Reference: Section 139(1) Income-tax Act
Penalty: Late filing can attract fee under Section 234F, interest and loss-related consequences.

Compliance: Income tax return — individual / HUF using ITR-3 or ITR-4, as applicable
Due Date: Annual — non-audit and audit cases have different statutory due dates; the product must determine audit applicability and tax period before generating the deadline.
Statutory Reference: Section 139(1) Income-tax Act
Penalty: Late filing can attract fee under Section 234F, interest and restrictions on carry-forward of certain losses.

Due Date: Correction — use the revised-return deadline applicable to the relevant assessment/tax year under the governing Act and current Finance Act amendments. Do not hard-code 31 December across years.
Statutory Reference: Section 139(5) Income-tax Act
Penalty: No separate penalty merely for a valid revision; interest / tax consequences continue to apply to the corrected return.

Due Date: Event-based — may be filed within the statutory updated-return window, currently extending up to 48 months from the end of the relevant assessment year, subject to eligibility
Statutory Reference: Section 139(8A) Income-tax Act r/w applicable updated-return provisions
Penalty: Additional income-tax is payable at the prescribed rate; eligibility restrictions apply.

Due Date: Annual / late filing — use the belated-return deadline applicable to the relevant assessment/tax year under the governing Act and current Finance Act amendments. Do not hard-code 31 December across years.
Statutory Reference: Section 139(4) Income-tax Act
Penalty: Late filing fee, interest and restrictions on carry-forward of certain losses may apply.

Due Date: Event-based — pay tax, interest and fee due before furnishing the return of income
Statutory Reference: Section 140A Income-tax Act
Penalty: Interest and other return-filing consequences may continue until outstanding tax is paid.

Compliance: Income-tax payment — demand / regular tax / other payment
Due Date: Event-based — by the due date stated in the applicable demand, order or statutory provision
Statutory Reference: Income-tax Act and applicable demand / payment provision
Penalty: Interest, recovery action and other consequences depend on the underlying tax liability.

Due Date: Annual — 6 months, up to day 30 of that month after end of the period
Statutory Reference: Section 44AB Income-tax Act r/w Rule 6G
Penalty: 0.5% of turnover, capped at ₹1,50,000, under Section 271B.

Due Date: Annual — 6 months, up to day 30 of that month after end of the period
Statutory Reference: Section 44AB Income-tax Act r/w Rule 6G
Penalty: 0.5% of turnover, capped at ₹1,50,000, under Section 271B.

Due Date: Annual / ongoing — maintain contemporaneous documentation by the return / report due date and retain it for the prescribed period
Statutory Reference: Section 92D Income-tax Act r/w Rule 10D Income-tax Rules
Penalty: Failure to maintain / furnish prescribed information can attract transfer-pricing penalties.

Penalty: Delay or non-filing can affect registration, exemption or deduction eligibility.
